LESSON: ISLAM IN EAST AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: History of Islam and Civilisation
Topic 7.1: Islam in East Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Islam in East Africa, part of History of Islam and Civilisation in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How are Muslims affected in East Africa? 2. How can Muslims come out of the challenges they face in East Africa?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or on available reference materials the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Tanzania and Uganda up to the 19th century and make notes,

2. brainstorm on the social, political and economic impacts of Islam in Tanzania and Uganda and present in class,

3. research on the challenges facing Muslims Tanzania and Uganda in the 21st century and make summary notes,

4. discuss possible solutions to address the challenges 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or on available reference materials the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Tanzania and Uganda up to the 19th century and make notes,
2. brainstorm on the social, political and economic impacts of Islam in Tanzania and Uganda and present in class,
3. research on the challenges facing Muslims Tanzania and Uganda in the 21st century and make summary notes,
4. discuss possible solutions to address the challenges 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Islam in East Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: the skills of interacting with digital technology and connecting with technology enhanced as learners

search online for the factors that led to the spread of Islam in Africa (Tanzania Uganda) up to the 19th century and make

notes

• Communication and Collaboration: the skills of listening, speaking, writing and teamwork enhanced as learners brainstorm

on the social, political and economic impacts of Islam in Africa (Tanzania, Uganda,) and present in class

• Learning to learn: the skill of carrying out research enhanced as learners research on the challenges facing the Muslims in

Africa (Tanzania, Uganda, Nigeria and Egypt) in the 21st century and make summary notes
